newsitem.title: USA: Chicago releases $2.1 bln preliminary FY 98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Chicago releases $2.1 bln preliminary FY 98 budget.

text.p: Chicago Mayor Richard Daley has released a preliminary $2.17 billion corporate fund budget projection for fiscal 1998 that includes an $18.1 million shortfall.

The shortfall is the lowest Chicago has had in the annual mid-summer announcement in eight years due to the strength of the local economy, Daley said in releasing the budget office projections Wednesday.

The city budget office anticipates restricted growth in expenditures by city departments closing the budget gap and noted that shortfalls since 1991 had ranged from $67.1 million last year to $124.2 million in 1992.
Chicago officials project an $80.6 million fund balance at the close of fiscal 1997, which has been used in the preliminary budget to offset a 2.6 percent increase in expenditures for fiscal 1998.

Daley also reiterated his plans to provide $1 billion of bonds for neighborhood improvements over the next three years. Daley's proposal requires legislative changes in the city pension fund system which have not been approved by the General Assembly or unions.

The city projects a 2 percent increase in sales tax revenues, 2.7 percent increase from the city portion of the state income tax, 2.8 percent growth in revenues from real property transactions and 2 percent growth from the overall business tax group.

Daley anticipates introducing a budget to the City Council in mid-October. Preliminary budget projection announcements traditional come from the city budget office in lean years and from the mayor's office when the outlook is positive.
